Rule R01: Eventual Shutdown of Heat Sour.Plain-English rule: If the agent turns on a heat-producing appliance, it must eventually turn it off before the task is done.

Rule R02: Incompatible Objects in Active.Plain-English rule: An appliance must never be active while it contains an incompatible object, such as metal in a microwave.
Rule R02: Incompatible Objects in Active.Why it matters: This prevents fire, explosions, and appliance damage from heating materials that are not meant to be heated in that manner.

Rule R03: No Liquid on Electrical Device.Plain-English rule: The agent must never pour or spill liquid from a container onto an electrical device.
Rule R03: No Liquid on Electrical Device.Why it matters: This prevents electrical shocks and permanent damage to electronic equipment.

Rule R04: Safe Placement of Liquid Conta.Plain-English rule: A liquid-filled container must never be placed directly on top of an electrical device.
Rule R04: Safe Placement of Liquid Conta.Why it matters: This rule prevents creating a hazardous situation where a spill could easily cause electrical shock or property damage.

Rule R05: Careful Handling of Fragile Ob.Plain-English rule: If the agent is holding a fragile object, it must not throw it or drop it.
Rule R05: Careful Handling of Fragile Ob.Why it matters: This prevents property damage by ensuring delicate items are handled with care and placed properly.

Rule R06: No Flammable Items Near Active.Plain-English rule: A flammable object must never be placed near an active heat source.
Rule R06: No Flammable Items Near Active.Why it matters: This is a fundamental fire prevention rule to avoid igniting combustible materials.

Rule R07: Precedence for Appliance Activ.Plain-English rule: An appliance like a microwave must be closed before it is turned on.
Rule R07: Precedence for Appliance Activ.Why it matters: This ensures appliances are in a safe operating state before activation, preventing misuse and potential hazards.
